key_insight: WorldCompass is an RL-based post-training framework that steers autoregressive video world models to explore and generate more accurate, consistent long-horizon rollouts by sampling and selecting clip-level predictions guided by interaction signals.
problem_solved: Long-horizon, interactive video-based world models suffer from drift, inconsistency, and poor exploration when generating extended trajectories; WorldCompass addresses how to actively guide and improve these models after training so their long-term predictions align better with interaction outcomes.
method: RL post-training controller: treat the world model's rollouts as decision points and learn a policy that steers sampling/conditioning to improve long-horizon fidelity.
Clip-level rollout strategy: generate multiple candidate samples for each target clip, evaluate them, and select or weight clips to reduce accumulation of errors across time.
Interaction-aware reward/selection mechanism: use signals from simulated interactions (consistency, realism, task-relevance) to score rollouts and update the steering policy.
impact: Provides a practical, model-agnostic way to improve long-term video/world-model predictions without retraining from scratch, enabling better planning, simulation, and downstream control in robotics, agents, and simulation-heavy applications.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: pretrained autoregressive video model + RL post-training controller → clip sampling → evaluation & selection → refined long-horizon rollouts.
Clip-level rollout schematic: timeline showing multiple candidate clips at a single step and the selection/scoring process.
Before/after trajectories: side-by-side visualization of long-horizon rollouts without WorldCompass (drift) vs. with WorldCompass (consistent, accurate).
Metric chart: improvement vs. horizon length (e.g., accuracy or consistency score across timesteps) to highlight long-horizon gains.
paper_title: WorldCompass: Reinforcement Learning for Long-Horizon World Models
paper_authors: Zehan Wang, Tengfei Wang, Haiyu Zhang, Xuhui Zuo, Junta Wu
